## Welcome

This standalone site contains the Kaikoria Valley College Urban Farm units 2026. The units are designed to be used in the context of the school farm, providing students with practical applications of agriculture and horticulture while exploring mathematical concepts through real-world scenarios.

## Course Overview

This course aligns with Te Mataiaho, the Refreshed New Zealand Curriculum [@moe-refreshed-nzc], and supports learners as they connect mathematical thinking with practical farm contexts. None of the content here is intended to be used as a standalone mathematics course, but rather as a way to explore mathematics in the context of agriculture and horticulture. The units are designed to be flexible and adaptable to different learning environments, allowing teachers to tailor the content to their students' needs.

No connection to the school farm is required to use the units, but teachers are encouraged to explore ways to connect the content to their own local contexts. The units are designed to be flexible and adaptable, allowing teachers to tailor the content to their students' needs.

Not endorsed by the Ministry of Education, but designed to support teachers and students in exploring mathematics in the context of agriculture and horticulture.

### Units

Each unit is designed to provide students with practical applications of agriculture and horticulture in the context of our school farm. The sequence supports the direction of current curriculum and assessment changes in Aotearoa New Zealand [@moe-ncea-change]. Each unit focuses on a specific aspect of farm operations, allowing students to experience real maintenance tasks and develop new skills at the same time as they explore pathways to agriculture and horticulture in New Zealand. As an added benefit, students will also engage with mathematical concepts through real-world scenarios.
